correctness.rationale: Every nonzero polynomial has positive radial mass on each side of the cutoff; negative covariance under size bias yields strict Rayleigh-quotient decrease. Compactness of projective polynomial space makes the decrease uniform, and minimax gives each ordered angular eigenvalue inequality. Negative sectors embed radially into positive counterparts. For the unweighted bianalytic case, explicit full and partial Gram matrices give trace T_k and determinant R^(2k+4); polynomial evaluations at R^2 order all top modes. Exact eigenvectors, the spectral theorem, and characteristic expansions prove the sharp gap and endpoint coefficients. The 1,812 packaged checks validate finite computations but do not replace these proofs.

value.rationale: For every polyanalytic order and every positive radial weight the theorem reduces a genuinely matrix-valued infinite-mode disk concentration problem to a finite radial moment pencil and identifies all maximizing directions as radial. For the natural first nonanalytic case, it additionally gives every eigenvalue, both leading eigendirections, the optimal global concentration-stability coefficient and its exact cubic boundary scale. These are structurally meaningful robustness and localization facts, beyond a routine single-matrix substitution; generalized off-center/annular masks are explicitly excluded.
